sector_model: Online marketplace: P/E, FCF after capex, SBC, net debt, GMV and take rate; acquisition effects (Depop).
thesis: eBay (Nasdaq: EBAY), online marketplace. Q3 2026 10-Q (filed 2026-10-29) read. Q3 net revenues 3,206M (+14%, +13% FX-neutral) and GMV 23,166M (+15%); 9M revenues 9,429M (+16%); take rate 13.84% vs 14.03%. Depop (C2C fashion) bought 2026-07-30 for 1.4B cash. Q3 net income 497M vs 628M: Q3 2025 had a 25M tax benefit versus a 104M provision now (effective rate 17.1% vs -4.3%), while sales and marketing rose 23% (747M vs 606M). Close 115.59 (2026-11-20) x 439M shares (cover, 2026-10-23) = 50.7B = 24.2x TTM NI 2,099M (2,031-1,491+1,559); TTM FCF 2,412M (OCF 3,049 less capex 637) = 4.8%; SBC 9M 511M. Debt 6,733M (short-term 1,599 + long-term 5,134) vs cash and investments 4,146M; equity 4,412M after heavy buybacks (9M repurchases 1,509M). The 9M 2025 OCF was depressed by 1,090M working capital outflows, so TTM FCF is flattered by a base effect.
counterthesis: TTM FCF yield of 4.8% partly reflects a weak 2025 working capital base; SBC of about 0.7B a year is roughly 28% of FCF. Q3 profit fell despite 14% revenue growth as marketing spend and the tax rate rose; take rate fell. Depop adds integration risk and 1.4B of cash spend while short-term debt doubled to 1,599M. Growth is partly acquired. Stock was 125.15 on Nov 4 and 115.59 on Nov 20 (-7.6%), cause not established. Price is about 46% above its Feb 2026 low of 79.41 (Yahoo), so much of the rerating already happened.
invalidation: Downgrade if take rate and GMV growth slow while marketing spend keeps rising, or Depop dilutes margins; upgrade case needs verified peers (AMZN, ETSY, MELI), normalized cash flow, MD&A and verified quote origins.
